CANONICAL_NAME.value: py_vollib + py_lets_be_rational -- Black-Scholes(-Merton) pricing and Jaeckel's 'Let's Be Rational' implied volatility (vollib)

VERSION.value: github.com/vollib/py_vollib master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes); py_lets_be_rational from PyPI at run time (recorded)

value.lineage: Option pricing (Black & Scholes 1973; Merton 1973) and the inverse problem -- implied volatility -- solved to machine precision in two iterations by Peter Jaeckel's 'Let's Be Rational' (2013/2015), a precision-engineering algorithm (rational approximations per branch, careful handling of extreme moneyness). vollib wraps Jaeckel's reference C++ as Python (py_lets_be_rational is the translation).

value.built_to: price European options and, more demandingly, recover the volatility a market price implies, to full double precision, in constant time
value.pressure: markets quoting prices at extreme strikes where naive root-finders lose all digits or fail to converge; latency budgets
value.success_means: the round trip price -> implied vol -> price closes to ~1e-12 across the grid

value.pressure: numerical ill-conditioning at extreme moneyness, latency
value.failure_condition: the inversion fails or returns a volatility off by percent for deep out-of-the-money options

ANCESTRY.value: Option pricing (Black & Scholes 1973; Merton 1973) and the inverse problem -- implied volatility -- solved to machine precision in two iterations by Peter Jaeckel's 'Let's Be Rational' (2013/2015), a precision-engineering algorithm (rational approximations per branch, careful handling of extreme moneyness). vollib wraps Jaeckel's reference C++ as Python (py_lets_be_rational is the translation).
